cells.tense: Right now you are holding the pen and the compass is already reading true.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Go back to something that ended and name what it left you — a skill, a lesson, a fact of having survived it. Don't weigh it against what it cost. Just keep the count.
cells.core:
When the inner sense of what's owed is working, you don't need to stop and calculate. You know the fair call in the moment and it moves you straight into the next step. The goal doesn't get built on self-doubt; it gets built on a felt rightness that holds even when no one is watching.

The harvest part comes when something has already ended. You gather what the ending left behind — the skill, the lesson, the quieter fact of having survived it — and that yield is what feeds the next goal. It isn't nostalgic and it isn't a ledger. You're just taking what's ripe and carrying it forward.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair, and that knowing moves you.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair, privately, as the compass for what gets done next
cells.place: Where your energy is aimed at a goal and carries you through resistance

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a fairness ruling that hasn't happened yet.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Find one person with something practical that needs doing for them. Do it, all the way, without adding advice or a fix for their life. When it's done, stop.
cells.core:
When this runs too hot, the inner compass starts grading outcomes before they arrive. You calculate whether a goal is fair before you've done it, whether a result will be deserved before you have it, and the reckoning runs out past the work. The drive is still there, but it's driving toward a verdict not yet reached, so every step costs more than it should.

Turn that weight outward instead — concretely. Give someone a real piece of help: carry the box, make the call, stay till the task is actually finished. Strength that holds without forcing pulls you down out of the grading in your head and back into the moment where you can move.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door you already walked through, and the compass has gone quiet.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Somebody near you is stuck on a path you happen to know. Go with them partway — say the turns as you go, in plain words, and stay until they can hold the route themselves.
cells.core:
When this runs low, the inner sense of fairness goes dim. You aren't checking what's right or owed; you're just pushing toward the goal with no compass reading at all. The drive is there, but it has no moral direction, so it drifts or stalls. You've left the present moment and the route you once knew feels like a door behind you.

Walking somebody else along it pulls the reading back. Go partway with someone who's lost, say the turns out loud as they come, and let that carry without forcing anything. Saying the way out loud reminds you that you can still see it, and it loosens the stalled place from the outside in.
cells.sheetLine: The compass has gone quiet and the drive has no direction.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair, privately, as the compass for what gets done next
cells.place: Where your energy is aimed at a goal and carries you through resistance

cells.tense: You are steering by a compass you don't know you're holding.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: For a week, when a pull lands on you — a goal, an obligation, a want — pause for one breath and ask whose it actually is. Mark the answer somewhere or not. Decide whether to keep it or set it down. No finish line.
cells.core:
The fair sense is running the show without being claimed. You make calls about what's right and what's owed all day, and the calls are good, but you'd tell anyone that you're just doing what's practical. The compass is steering, and you're saying you're only following the route.

Noticing over time returns it, not more analysis. Put the pulls on you side by side when they arrive — the goals you're chasing, the obligations, the things you want — and sort one from the next. Discernment here lets several truths sit together without collapsing them. It's quieter than driving, and it hands the wheel back without a fight.
cells.sheetLine: The compass is steering while you say you're just following.
cells.verb: Weighing what is fair, privately, as the compass for what gets done next
cells.place: Where your energy is aimed at a goal and carries you through resistance
